The Nemotron example warms up once (which also fills the tune store), then times and profiles a second run, printing its per-kernel report: cargo run -p svod-model --release --example nemotron_diarize -- audio_1.wav --dtype bf16 --profile tk kernels appear under their kernel names (gemm, conv, flash_attention, heads, layer_norm, …) next to graph kernels, timed the same way. Measure on a quiet GPU Another process on the GPU skews every number. The probes and the tune store warm the clock first. Run probes with --test-threads=1.

Each op ranks its configs per shape in ops::config from the device's measured costs (see Device costs), dropping the configs priced past 2.5× the cheapest once 16 tiles are kept (config::PRUNED_PAST): on sm_86 none of them ran within the contender band. The ranking is a model, and so is a register count, so neither admits a config. One rule does: the tuner compiles the ranked configs in parallel until it has the first 64 tiles in ranked order (config::SHORTLIST) whose compiled kernels do not spill (a kernel reporting scratch bytes spilled; a backend that reports nothing admits). A tile is admitted at its first clean pipeline (ring depth, unrolling), so an unrolled ring that spills yields to its rolled twin. A pipeline is compiled only when the tile's pipelines ranked ahead of it spilled or failed, and none past the 64th clean tile: what a walk in ranked order compiling one config at a time would compile (config::Search). The tiles none of whose pipelines compile clean follow the clean ones within the 64, a pipeline each: the compiled kernel judges what it can and the time the rest (no op falls to the graph because of spills, and on gfx1201 the 16384² depth-768 nearest's best tile spills 196 bytes a lane and runs 2 % ahead of the clean pick). A config's compile starts as soon as the search wants it, on the thread pool (where the pool has room, a tile's next pipeline starts while the one ahead still compiles, its verdict used only where the walk would have asked for it); one whose compiler runs past 30 s (tune::COMPILE_TIMEOUT) is killed and rejected as a failure would be, and the planner log says so (compile timed out); one whose lowered program emits more instructions than its target may (Target::most_instructions: 2^18 on AMD, 2^19 on CUDA, above the largest ranked kernels) is refused by the lowering before any compiler sees it (lower::Error::TooLarge, does not lower in the planner log) and rejected alike. Each program is lowered once per tuning: what the store's fingerprint lowered is the body the compile launches. The admitted configs, with their variants (key splits for attention, reduction splits for a starved convolution), are the candidates the tune store measures the first time a device meets a shape. The other pipelines of the leading tiles, those within the contender band of the leader and at most eight (config::TWIN_TILES), are then compiled and timed against the winner, spilling or not, and the fastest is the choice. Attention tunes its softmax forms and its tiles in turn (see the Kernel Library). When nothing compiles (no device to compile on) the first 64 tiles are used untested. With tuning off nothing is timed: the ranked list's first config that compiles clean runs, found compiling in ranked batches of eight and kept in the store as a first line. The device's cost probes still measure, since the ranking needs them.

The op measures where it is called, while the graph is built, never inside a running plan. Each candidate is built as a program, launched on scratch buffers at capacity with every runtime variable bound to its maximum (float operands hold values drawn in [-1, 1), so a card that clocks down under real data is timed as it will run; integer operands hold zeros), and timed: Step Setting Warm-up Back-to-back runs until the clock plateaus Rounds One round of every candidate in ranked order, where a candidate whose first timed run passes 2× the best so far keeps that run as its time; then 3 more of the contenders: those within 1.2× of the first round's best (within 2×, under 8 candidates), each round past the second only those within 1.05× of the best so far, the later rounds running backwards and forwards in turn so that each candidate runs after both its neighbours; then 4 more of the two leaders, where more than two contenders ran. The first timing of a tuning, which only picks its leading tiles, stops after the second round: those tiles are timed again with their other pipelines Per round 5 ms of device time in back-to-back sustain runs of the candidate's programs in order (at most 1024 launches, sized by the candidate's last run), then profiled runs of each program, keeping each candidate's minimum: as many as 20 ms of device time holds, 2 to 5 (tune::runs), and no sustain for a candidate of 5 ms or more, whose first timed run then counts among them; the leaders' rounds (and the cost probes) keep 5 runs after a sustain Time of a run The sum of its kernels' GPU timestamps The sustain is sized in device time because launches queue asynchronously. A candidate is a list of programs, a kernel plus the merge of its partial results for a split, and its time is the sum of its programs' times. Candidates not compiled yet when a timing starts (a split's variants, a tile's twins) compile on all but one of the pool's threads while the ones ready are timed, each timed when the ranked order reaches it. A candidate that fails to build or run is skipped. If nothing measures, the first candidate is used and nothing is stored. Two guards keep a time honest: One device lock. Every timing in the process, the tuner's and the cost probes' alike, holds one lock: two measurements sharing the device would time each other. Two threads tuning the same key measure it once; the second waits for the first's answer. The stamp guard. A run under half the median of its candidate's runs is a lost stamp and is dropped before the fastest is kept, for the tuner and the probes alike.

What Value Directory $SVOD_TK_TUNE_DIR, else $XDG_CACHE_HOME/svod/tk_tune, else ~/.cache/svod/tk_tune File One per device and crate version, e.g. sm_86_28sm-v0.2.0.txt, headed by its line format (format 5); a file of another format, or without the line, is dropped whole Line kind|op|device|dtype|shape|candidates|compiler|programs numbers: a choice holds the candidates that ran, fastest first, each index ns (a candidate whose programs emit what another's do — an unrolling the schedule folds away — is recorded at its twin's ns, the kernel the two share); a value a measured number; an admitted the ranked indices admission kept; a first the first clean config's index Key tune::TuneKey { op, device, dtype, shape, candidates, compiler }, where device is arch and SM count (sm_86-28sm) and compiler digests the device's compiler (tune::compiler) Lines from a real store on the RTX 3060: an attention choice (shape [batch, t, tk, heads, kv_heads, d], candidate 0 at 3904 ns) and a cost probe's value (femtoseconds per unit). choice|attention|sm_86-28sm|BFloat16|2x10x12x6x2x64|08bd45c243ff1581|9154cc72f03d25cd|ef103f71226add50 0 3904 1 3936 value|probe:cached_1m|sm_86-28sm|Int32||0a2d6c02b82988af|9154cc72f03d25cd|d2a8e296bcce85e4 16601 The programs field fingerprints the kernels the candidates emit: the lowered program and the LLVM text the backend is handed, so a change to the kernels or the renderer re-measures and a refactor that emits the same kernels does not. What a program emits is remembered by what it is made of, per build of the executable, in emitted/<build>.txt under the store's root (a build unused for a week is removed), so a warm process of the same build lowers nothing and a rebuild lowers each program once. Only a store miss compiles. Writes re-read, merge and atomically replace the file. An unreadable or unwritable store counts as a miss, never an error.

The ranking's costs (atoms::Costs: a shared byte, a streamed byte, a scattered element, a matrix-core step under a full SM, alone on its SIMD and as a warpgroup product, a score's softmax, a pipeline trip over two ring slots unrolled and rolled and over one, the two-slot and one-slot trips of a block alone on its SM, a lane move, a shared round trip, the global latency through two ring slots and, where fills are cp.async, through one, and the L2 rate and size) are measured on the device by probe::costs the first time a process plans for it. Each field is a pair of programs, a probe doing all its baseline does plus a known amount of the primitive. The values go in the same store file as value|probe:<field> lines, so later processes read them back. A probe that fails leaves its field at zero, is warned about, and is named in Planner::unmeasured, which the device gate device_costs_are_physical holds empty: the planner ranks with what it has rather than leaving the device to the graph. Only a device without an SM count has no planner. Host tests declare costs instead (test::unit::costs(), and gfx1151_costs() pasted from a gfx1151 store). For a card this machine has no device for, Target::offline or Target::card gives the target, and probe::stored reads the costs from a tune store copied from that card; without one, probe::GUESSED stands in and the ranking is a guess. The tk_dump example does both.

RUST_LOG=svod_tk::plan=debug logs the planner's decisions: an op that takes the graph and why, a ranking's first 16 configs with their predicted ns and how many configs it left out, on a store miss what compiling each config showed (verdict, registers, spilled bytes), and the tuned pick. RUST_LOG=svod_tk=debug adds the tuner's rounds.

How Effect SVOD_TK_TUNE=0 Candidate timing off; the first ranked config that compiles clean runs (kept as a first line); the cost probes still measure svod_tk::tune::scoped(false, f) The same for f on this thread (and the workers it compiles on), over the environment; tests use it tune::TuneStore::at(root) builds a store at another root, or in memory only with None.

The probe tests are #[ignore] tests that print timings and never assert. They rank with the device's probed costs and time the shortlist the tuner admits, marking the tuner's pick.
